title_zh: 印度儿童急性脑炎综合征的病因谱:系统评价和荟萃分析。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) continues to be an important cause of illness and death among children in India. While Japanese encephalitis (JE) virus has traditionally been regarded as the leading cause, recent studies indicate that the range of causative organisms has widened considerably. AIM: To estimate the pooled proportion of AES cases attributable to various common infectious etiologies among children aged 18 years or younger in India. METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted for studies published between January 2000 and December 2025. Studies conducted in India that included at least 25 children (≤ 18 years) with AES and reported laboratory-confirmed etiologies were considered eligible. Case reports and small case series were excluded. Quality assessment of included studies was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. A random-effects model was used to obtain pooled estimates and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: A total of 69 studies were included in the final analysis. Scrub typhus emerged as the most common cause, accounting for 20% (95%CI: 13%-27%) of AES cases, followed by JE at 13% (95%CI: 11%-15%). Enterovirus accounted for 6% of the cases (95%CI: 3%-9%). Dengue, herpes simplex virus and Epstein-Barr virus accounted for 5% of the cases each (95%CI: 3%-8%, 2%-9%, and 1%-11%, respectively). Mumps and chikungunya virus accounted for 4% each (95%CI: 1%-8%, and 2%-5%, respectively). CONCLUSION: Scrub typhus and JE are the leading identifiable etiology of pediatric AES in India. Broader diagnostic methods, including molecular techniques, may improve the diagnostic yield and facilitate early targeted therapy in children with AES.
abstract_zh: 背景:急性脑炎综合征(AES)仍然是印度儿童患病和死亡的重要原因。虽然日本脑炎(JE)病毒传统上被认为是主要原因,但最近的研究表明,致病微生物的范围已大大扩大。目的:估计印度 18 岁或以下儿童中由各种常见感染病因引起的 AES 病例的汇总比例。方法:对 PubMed/MEDLINE、EMBASE 和 Scopus 进行全面检索,查找 2000 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间发表的研究。在印度进行的研究,包括至少 25 名患有 AES 的儿童(≤ 18 岁),并报告了实验室确认的病因,被认为是合格的。病例报告 和小箱系列被排除在外。使用乔安娜布里格斯研究所清单对纳入的研究进行质量评估。使用随机效应模型来获得汇总估计值及其相应的 95% 置信区间 (CI)。结果:共有69项研究纳入最终分析。恙虫病是最常见的病因,占 AES 病例的 20%(95%CI:13%-27%),其次是乙脑,占 13%(95%CI:11%-15%)。肠道病毒占病例的 6%(95%CI:3%-9%)。登革热、单纯疱疹病毒和 Epstein-Barr 病毒各占病例的 5%(95%CI:分别为 3%-8%、2%-9% 和 1%-11%)。腮腺炎和 基孔肯雅病毒 各占 4%(95%CI:分别为 1%-8% 和 2%-5%)。结论:恙虫病和乙型脑炎是印度儿童 AES 的主要可识别病因。更广泛的诊断方法,包括分子技术,可以提高 AES 儿童的诊断率并促进早期靶向治疗。

title: Molecular Cloning and Reverse Genetics.
abstract: This chapter describes a detailed molecular biology protocol for introducing specific point mutations into the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome using a reverse genetics strategy. The method utilizes an overlapping PCR-based approach to generate a mutated DNA fragment, which is then cloned into a pre-engineered CHIKV infectious clone plasmid. The protocol covers all major steps, from the initial PCRs to create the mutated insert to its digestion and ligation into the vector. It also includes procedures for bacterial transformation, colony screening via PCR and Sanger sequencing to confirm the mutation, and plasmid purification via miniprep. The document is structured with a clear introduction, a list of all required reagents and equipment, and a step-by-step methods section.

title: Screening of Antiviral Agents Against CHIKV Using Reporter Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes a disease characterized by chronic musculoskeletal inflammation for which specific antivirals are not yet available. Currently, a supportive therapy to alleviate fever and pain is used, but it does not limit viral replication or the persistence of chronic arthritis symptoms. Thus, the identification and development of new active molecules against CHIKV is urgently needed. Here, we present a cell-based methodology that enables the implementation of a rapid and cost-effective strategy for high- and medium-throughput screening (HTS) of compounds, including repurposed drugs or novel molecules. This methodology allows for the identification of novel antiviral hits with a good activity and selectivity profile against CHIKV.

title: Epitope Tagging and Coimmunoprecipitation to Identify Viral Protein Interactors.
abstract: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) is a powerful proteomic approach for dissecting the interaction network between virus and host. Traditional AP-MS employs overexpression of viral proteins as baits to enrich host interactors. However, overexpressed viral proteins may mislocalize to inappropriate cellular compartments and trigger endoplasmic reticulum stress by overwhelming the protein-folding machinery, which leads to false identification of host factors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2), which we used to successfully uncover two new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs-macrophages. In this protocol, we will describe this technique step by step: (1) design and construction of myc-tagged virus by advanced multi-fragment assembly, (2) in vitro transcription and preparation of infectious myc-tagged virus stocks, and (3) immunoprecipitation of myc-tagged viral protein and its interactome for mass spectrometry analysis. This strategy enables accurate identification of viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, providing a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.

title_zh: 表位标记和免疫共沉淀鉴定病毒蛋白相互作用物。
source_body_en: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) is a powerful proteomic approach for dissecting the interaction network between virus and host. Traditional AP-MS employs overexpression of viral proteins as baits to enrich host interactors. However, overexpressed viral proteins may mislocalize to inappropriate cellular compartments and trigger endoplasmic reticulum stress by overwhelming the protein-folding machinery, which leads to false identification of host factors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2), which we used to successfully uncover two new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs-macrophages. In this protocol, we will describe this technique step by step: (1) design and construction of myc-tagged virus by advanced multi-fragment assembly, (2) in vitro transcription and preparation of infectious myc-tagged virus stocks, and (3) immunoprecipitation of myc-tagged viral protein and its interactome for mass spectrometry analysis. This strategy enables accurate identification of viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, providing a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.
abstract_zh: 亲和纯化质谱 (AP-MS) 是一种强大的蛋白质组学方法,用于剖析病毒和 宿主 之间的相互作用网络。传统的 AP-MS 采用病毒蛋白的过度表达作为诱饵来丰富 宿主 相互作用子。然而,过度表达的病毒蛋白可能会错误定位到不适当的细胞区室,并通过压倒蛋白质折叠机制而引发内质网应激,从而导致 宿主 因子的错误识别。为了克服这些限制,我们引入了一种基于直接感染表位标记的 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV/myc-E2) 的 AP-MS 策略,我们用它成功地发现了 CHIKV 细胞 储存宿主 巨噬细胞中的两个新的 抗病毒药物 因子。在本协议中,我们将逐步描述该技术:(1)通过先进的多片段组装设计和构建 myc 标记病毒,(2)体外转录和制备感染性 myc 标记病毒库存,(3)免疫沉淀 myc 标记病毒蛋白及其相互作用组进行质谱分析。该策略能够在生理相关背景下准确识别病毒相互作用因子,为未来使用标记病毒的蛋白质组学研究提供框架。

title: A Restriction-Free Cloning Approach for Molecular Engineering of Plasmids.
abstract: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.

title_zh: 质粒分子工程的无限制克隆方法。
source_body_en: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.
abstract_zh: 使用高持续性、高保真度 DNA 聚合酶通过 PCR 扩增进行分子克隆代表了一种用于精确操作核酸序列的稳健且通用的技术。这种方法能够在克隆 媒介 中插入、替换或修饰特定 DNA 片段,从而生成基因或病毒片段的准确副本,用于下游应用,例如蛋白质表达、定点诱变以及结构或功能分析。使用持续的高保真聚合酶可显着减少碱基替换错误的发生,确保整个扩增过程中的序列完整性。传统上,限制性内切酶被用来促进定向克隆。然而,替代方法允许诱变,而不需要独特和特定的限制位点,并且可以应用于几乎任何克隆或无缝 DNA 组装策略。在本章中,我们描述了一种基于无限制性内切酶和无连接 PCR 的方案,广泛适用于任何环状 媒介。该方法能够对 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 基因组 进行定向诱变,为生成适合病毒学和分子研究的突变体构建体提供快速、高效和可靠的策略。

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

title: Single‐cell transcriptomic analysis of the immune response to CHIKV infection
abstract: Abstract Background The Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, is responsible for acute febrile illness and severe polyarthralgia. Although both innate and adaptive immune responses influence the disease outcomes, the detailed cellular immunopathogenesis of CHIKV in peripheral blood is not yet fully elucidated. Methods We conducted single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) obtained from patients acutely infected with CHIKV and from healthy control subjects. Cellular interactions were inferred, and the transcriptomic results were orthogonally validated through quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) and Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) to assess systemic interferon-stimulated responses. Furthermore, a comparative analysis was performed using publicly available single-cell data from Dengue virus (DENV) infections. Results CHIKV infection significantly altered the immune system, increasing monocytes and dendritic cells while reducing T and B lymphocytes. Monocytes and NK cells showed strong activation of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Monocytes were identified as key in driving inflammatory and immune responses. In adaptive immunity, CHIKV led B cells to become plasmablasts with antiviral immunoglobulins and caused T cells and NK-like T cells to show signs of cytotoxicity and exhaustion. Validation showed increased levels of IFN-γ, IFN-β1, MX1, and ISG15. CHIKV triggered a more intense, monocyte-driven interferon response than DENV. Conclusions Acute CHIKV infection induces a systemic interferon response predominantly centered on monocytes, accompanied by significant alterations in adaptive immunity. Circulating ISG products, including MX1 and ISG15, reflect the transcriptomic activation and may serve as potential biomarkers for assessing the early intensity of innate antiviral responses.

source_records.title: Single‐cell transcriptomic analysis of the immune response to CHIKV infection
source_records.abstract: Background The Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, is responsible for acute febrile illness and severe polyarthralgia. Although both innate and adaptive immune responses influence the disease outcomes, the detailed cellular immunopathogenesis of CHIKV in peripheral blood is not yet fully elucidated. Methods We profiled PBMCs from 29 patients with acute CHIKV infection and 10 controls via single-cell RNA sequencing. Between-group analyses treated donors as biological replicates, incorporating pseudobulk differential expression analysis as well as donor-level comparisons of pathway scores and cell proportions. Orthogonal validation was performed using qPCR and ELISA, and an exploratory analysis was conducted on a publicly available DENV dataset. Results Interferon-response signatures were upregulated across the majority of PBMC populations, with particularly prominent signals observed in monocytes and NK cells. Differences in relative cell composition were detected in descriptive statistics, but did not retain statistical significance after donor-level multiple testing correction. B-cell immunoglobulin isotypes varied across cell subsets, and their transcripts did not allow determination of antigen specificity. Cross-study analysis of DENV did not support the quantitative conclusion that the CHIKV-induced immune response is stronger. Conclusions Acute CHIKV infection is associated with a broad interferon-stimulated transcriptional program in PBMCs. Conclusions drawn from cross-sectional and cross-study comparisons require cautious interpretation.

abstract_zh: 摘要背景 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 是一种重新出现的蚊媒甲病毒,可导致急性发热性疾病和严重的多关节痛。尽管先天性和适应性 免疫应答 都会影响疾病结果,但外周血中 CHIKV 的详细细胞免疫发病机制尚未完全阐明。方法 我们对从 CHIKV 急性感染患者和健康对照受试者中获得的外周血单核细胞 (PBMC) 进行了单细胞 RNA 测序 (scRNA-seq)。推断细胞相互作用,并通过定量实时 PCR (qPCR) 和酶联免疫吸附测定 (ELISA) 正交验证转录组结果,以评估全身干扰素刺激的反应。此外,使用公开的登革热病毒(DENV)感染的单细胞数据进行了比较分析。结果 CHIKV 感染显着改变了免疫系统,增加了单核细胞和树突状细胞,同时减少了 T 和 B 淋巴细胞。单核细胞和 NK 细胞表现出干扰素刺激基因 (ISG) 的强烈激活。单核细胞被认为是驱动炎症和 免疫应答 的关键。在适应性免疫中,CHIKV通过抗病毒药物免疫球蛋白引导B细胞变成浆母细胞,并导致T细胞和NK样T细胞表现出细胞毒性和衰竭的迹象。验证显示 IFN-γ、IFN-β1、MX1 和 ISG15 水平增加。CHIKV 比 DENV 引发更强烈的单核细胞驱动的干扰素反应。结论 急性 CHIKV 感染诱导主要集中在单核细胞的全身干扰素反应,并伴有适应性免疫的显着改变。循环 ISG 产品,包括 MX1 和 ISG15,反映转录组激活,并可作为评估先天 抗病毒药物 反应早期强度的潜在生物标志物。

title: UHPLC-DAD-HRMS2 Characterization of Novel Dihydrochalcone Conjugates From the Antiviral Mansoa hirsuta Extracts: Diagnostic Fragmentation Pathways and Dereplication of Oligomeric Polyphenols.
abstract: High-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) coupled with ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography (UHPLC) enables rapid characterization of complex polyphenolic constituents in medicinal plants. Mansoa hirsuta (Bignoniaceae), a neotropical liana traditionally used to treat infectious diseases, remains poorly characterized chemically. This study reports the comprehensive UHPLC-DAD-HRMS/MS profiling of ethanolic extracts from leaves, stems, and fruits, leading to the identification of 57 phenolic compounds, including 40 previously unreported flavonoid conjugates. Accurate mass measurements and diagnostic MS/MS fragmentation patterns enabled the structural characterization of five classes of dihydrochalcone-derived metabolites: dihydrochalcone-tyramine, -flavanone (mansoin-type), -flavan-3-ol, and -flavonol conjugates. Characteristic fragment ions, particularly those corresponding to the dihydrochalcone core and tyramine moiety, supported the annotation of novel oligomeric flavonoids. Organ-specific metabolite distribution revealed leaves enriched in Mansoin A-type heterotrimers, stems containing phenylethanoid glycosides and cinnamoyl-mangiferins, and fruits predominated by simpler dihydrochalcone-tyramine conjugates. All extracts exhibited low cytotoxicity (CC50 > 400 μg mL-1) and selective antiviral activity against Zika (ZIKV), chikungunya (CHIKV), Mayaro (MAYV), and dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2). The stem extract showed the highest selectivity against ZIKV (SI > 25.5), whereas the fruit extract displayed the greatest potency against DENV-2 (EC50 = 25.4 ± 1.2 μg mL-1; SI > 19.7). These findings expand the phytochemical knowledge of M. hirsuta, demonstrate the utility of HRMS-based metabolite profiling for dereplication of complex flavonoids, and provide diagnostic MS/MS fragmentation patterns applicable to the characterization of related oligomeric flavonoids in other plant species.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在表征毛须草提取物的化学成分,以用于潜在的 抗病毒药物 应用,解决了解其植物化学特征和 抗病毒药物 针对 基孔肯雅病毒 活性的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及对 Mansoa hirsuta 叶、茎和果实的乙醇提取物进行 UHPLC-DAD-HRMS/MS 分析,重点是鉴定新型酚类化合物及其在植物不同部位的分布。
elements_zh.methods: 使用高分辨率质谱 (HRMS) 与超高效液相色谱 (UHPLC) 相结合来分析提取物,通过精确的质量测量和诊断性 MS/MS 碎片模式,能够鉴定 57 种酚类化合物,其中包括 40 种以前未报告的黄酮类缀合物。
elements_zh.main_results: 器官特异性代谢物分布显示,叶子富含曼索因A型异三聚体,茎含有苯乙醇苷和肉桂酰芒果苷,果实主要由更简单的二氢查尔酮-酪胺缀合物组成。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 特征片段离子的鉴定,特别是那些对应于二氢查耳酮核心和酪胺部分的片段离子,支持了新型低聚黄酮类化合物的注释,证明了基于 HRMS 的分析对于复杂黄酮类化合物去复制的实用性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了诊断性 MS/MS 碎片模式,适用于其他植物物种中相关寡聚黄酮类化合物的表征,这可能有助于开发针对 基孔肯雅病毒 的 抗病毒药物 策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象级别的报告,虽然它展示了基于 HRMS 的分析的潜力,但由于缺乏详细的实验数据和验证,证据强度中等。

title: Molecular Surveillance for Oropouche, Mayaro, West Nile, and Saint Louis EncephalitisViruses, Brazil, 2019–2025
abstract: To assess the circulation of Oropouche, Mayaro, West Nile, and St. Louis encephalitis viruses, we tested samples from 824 patients with acute febrile illness, 3,484 mosquitoes, and 113 nonhuman primates from northern Minas Gerais, Brazil. All samples were negative for dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika virus. One imported Oropouche virus infection was detected.

title: Investigating Lethality of Mayaro Virus, O’nyong-nyong Virus, Ross River Virus, and Una Virus in an Immunodeficient Murine Model
abstract: Arthritogenic alphaviruses are mosquito-borne viruses characteristically associated with severe rheumatic disease and febrile illness. While this group of arboviruses house significant epidemic potential due to expanding competent vectors, host plasticity, and recombination events increasing infectivity, the median lethal dose (LD50) for many members remains limited or non-existent, thus restraining medical countermeasure (MCM) investigations. Mayaro virus (MAYV), o’nyong-nyong virus (ONNV), Una virus (UNAV), and Ross River virus (RRV) are four arthritogenic alphaviruses with epidemic potential. However, at the time of our study, no literature examining LD50 values for each virus in IFNAR-deficient mice, an effective model for characterizing disease severity and thus MCM potential, was available. In this study, we subcutaneously inoculated IFNAR-deficient mice with ranged doses of MAYV, ONNV, UNAV, or RRV to determine the LD50. However, we were unsuccessful upon finding complete lethality across all ranged doses for each virus. We further validated MCM potential in our MAYV model by prophylactically treating mice with neutralizing antibody (nAb) and examining clinical scores, weight loss, and survival rates. Our study serves as the first to examine the lethality of UNAV, MAYV, and RRV infection in an IFNAR-deficient mouse model and provides crucial lethal dose reference material for future MAYV, ONNV, UNAV, and RRV studies.

title: CARACTERIZAÇÃO BIOESTATÍSTICA DA EFICÁCIA DA VACINA CYD-TDV: IMPLEMENTAÇÃO NO PROGRAMA DE VACINAÇÃO DO ESTADO DO PARANÁ-BRASIL.
abstract: Vivemos em um país com epidemias frequentes de dengue, ano após ano. Muito se tem falado na mídia sobre essa doença, os sintomas, as formas de transmissão e principalmente, as maneiras de preveni-la, no entanto, apesar dos esforços dos agentes de saúde, a doença se tornou um problema de saúde pública, sendo responsável por milhares de pacientes em todo o mundo. Como se não bastasse, o mosquito adquiriu novos vírus, o que provocou uma das maiores epidemias, como a Zika e a Chikungunya. Desde então, as epidemias ocorreram frequentemente em todo o território nacional do Brasil.Dessa forma, após o surto de Zika, no ano de 2015, e as diversas epidemias sucessivas de Dengue, tornou-se um problema de saúde pública, o que possibilitou a urgência em descobrir e estudar uma vacina que estivesse ao alcance da eficácia e segurança necessárias para proteger o indivíduo dessa doença. Assim, a urgência dos laboratórios nas pesquisas desenvolvidas para a descoberta de uma vacina, que teria a eficácia comprovada para o vírus da dengue, em seus 4 sorotipos, DENV-1, 2, 3, 4, viabilizou uma possível falha em estudos clínicos que poderiam acarretar baixa eficácia e segurança para os pacientes submetidos a esse tipo de vacinação. Além disso, forneceu estudos bioestatísticos, que a longo prazo analisam a eficácia e segurança da vacina CYD-TDV em uma determinada região onde foi introduzida.

analysis.research_question_and_background: O estudo busca compreender a eficácia e segurança da vacina CYD-TDV contra o vírus da dengue, considerando a necessidade de proteger a população diante de surtos frequentes e a emergência de novos vírus como a Zika e a Chikungunya.
analysis.study_design_and_population: O estudo foi conduzido em uma região específica do Brasil, com a implementação da vacina CYD-TDV no programa de vacinação do Estado do Paraná, visando analisar sua eficácia e segurança em uma população exposta a epidemias de dengue e outros vírus relacionados.
analysis.methods: Foram utilizados estudos bioestatísticos para avaliar a eficácia e segurança da vacina CYD-TDV, com análise de dados coletados ao longo de um período prolongado, considerando a introdução da vacina em uma determinada região e suas implicações epidemiológicas.
analysis.main_results: Os estudos bioestatísticos demonstraram a eficácia e segurança da vacina CYD-TDV em relação ao vírus da dengue, com resultados que indicaram uma proteção significativa contra os sorotipos DENV-1, 2, 3 e 4.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A interpretação dos resultados sugere que a vacina CYD-TDV é uma ferramenta eficaz para a prevenção da dengue, com uma nova abordagem na análise de sua eficácia em uma região específica do Brasil.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Os achados podem informar políticas públicas de vacinação e contribuir para a vigilância epidemiológica, especialmente em regiões com alta incidência de dengue e outros vírus relacionados.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A evidência é baseada em estudos bioestatísticos, o que pode limitar a generalização dos resultados para outras regiões ou populações, mas a análise foi conduzida com uma amostra representativa e confiável.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of the CYD-TDV vaccine against dengue virus, particularly in the context of frequent outbreaks and the emergence of related viruses such as Zika and Chikungunya. The research was conducted in the state of Paraná, Brazil, focusing on the implementation of the vaccine within the vaccination program. Bio-statistical analyses were employed to assess the vaccine's performance over an extended period, highlighting its effectiveness against the four dengue serotypes. The findings suggest that the vaccine is a valuable tool for dengue prevention, offering insights into its application in regions with high dengue incidence. However, the study's reliance on bio-statistical data may limit its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the specific regional focus and the need for further validation in diverse populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the withdrawal of the IXCHIQ chikungunya vaccine from the UK market following a safety review. The research aimed to inform public health and regulatory decisions regarding the vaccine's safety and efficacy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a review of safety data for the IXCHIQ chikungunya vaccine, conducted in the UK. The review was based on post-marketing surveillance data and safety reports.
analysis.methods: The methods included a review of safety data from post-marketing surveillance and safety reports. No specific sampling, assays, or statistical analyses were performed.
analysis.main_results: The results indicated that the IXCHIQ chikungunya vaccine was withdrawn from the UK market due to safety concerns identified during the post-marketing surveillance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating the need for ongoing safety monitoring of the vaccine and highlighted the importance of thorough safety reviews before and after vaccine approval.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against the use of the IXCHIQ chikungunya vaccine in the UK and emphasize the importance of continuous safety surveillance for vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on post-marketing surveillance data and the absence of specific methodological details. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: The IXCHIQ chikungunya vaccine was withdrawn from the UK market following a safety review. The study reviewed post-marketing surveillance data, indicating the need for ongoing safety monitoring and emphasizing the importance of thorough safety reviews.

full_text: Abstract Chikungunya, a mosquito-borne viral disease caused by Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), infects humans through the bite of Aedes sp. mosquitoes, causing high fever. Diagnosis includes the detection of IgM antibodies against CHIKV by ELISA. Department of Health Research (DHR)—Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) implemented an External Quality Assurance Scheme (EQAS) through Proficiency Testing (PT) to ensure the accuracy and reliability of CHIKV-IgM-ELISA testing across a network of laboratories in India. The geographical distribution of the participant laboratories from the PT provider (PTP) can lead to delayed transportation while distributing the PT panels, which could result in disqualification of PT panels due to suspected sample degradation and thus necessitates expensive panel redistributions. This study evaluated panel quality by assessing homogeneity and stability across various temperatures and time periods that simulate real-world transit conditions. The results were analyzed in accordance with ISO 13528:2022. This study shows that the CHIKV-positive samples in the PT panel remained robust across all tested temperature ranges and time periods, maintaining 100% qualitative concordance for up to 168 h and at a maximum temperature of 45 °C. Therefore, we conclude that the PT panels sent for EQA for the qualitative Chikungunya IgM ELISA test will be suitable for testing at the participant laboratories when received within a time duration of 168 h with a maximum transit temperature of 45 °C. Thus, the rejection of panels due to suspected sample degradation and expensive panel redistribution can be avoided. Data availability No datasets were generated or analyzed during the current study. title_original: Homogeneity and stability evaluation of EQA serum samples for Chikungunya IgM ELISA

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the homogeneity and stability of external quality assurance (EQA) serum samples for Chikungunya IgM ELISA to address the challenge of sample degradation during transit, which could affect diagnostic accuracy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted by the Department of Health Research (DHR)—Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) through an External Quality Assurance Scheme (EQAS) using proficiency testing (PT) panels distributed to a network of laboratories in India. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the homogeneity and stability of EQA serum samples for Chikungunya IgM ELISA under simulated real-world transit conditions. The research aimed to address the issue of sample degradation during transportation, which could lead to the disqualification of PT panels and necessitate costly redistributions. The study found that CHIKV-positive samples remained robust across all tested temperature ranges and time periods, maintaining 100% qualitative concordance for up to 168 hours at a maximum temperature of 45°C. These results suggest that the PT panels can be reliably used for EQA if received within these parameters, offering specific guidance for quality assurance programs. The study was conducted using leftover, de-identified samples, which may limit generalizability, but the findings are supported by ISO 13528:2022 standards, indicating strong evidence. The results have implications for improving the reliability of serological testing in field settings and reducing logistical challenges in quality assurance schemes.

title: Global patterns of genetic diversity and evolution in chikungunya virus E2 glycoprotein
abstract: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis were applied to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, we performed spatial–temporal stratification and analysis to assess clustering patterns across lineages and regions using Fixation index test (Fst). Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CKIKV E2 lineages (negatively statistically significant Tajima D, Fu and Li’s D, and Fu and Li’s F tests, p -values < 0.05) supported by codon‐based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint across the E2 gene but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage‐specific sites, notably codon 146 in the West African lineage, codons 220, 245, 247, and 254 in the Asian lineage, and codons 54, 56, 102, 145, 163, 177, and 350 in the East/Central/South/African lineage. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories. Haplotype network analysis highlighted distinct clustering patterns shaped by geography and epidemic waves, reflecting the persistence of lineage-specific signatures across regions. At the same time, reduced connectivity among recent outbreak strains point to more discrete intercontinental movement events, likely driven by human-mediated vector dispersal or travel-associated introductions. Collectively, these findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the genetic diversity and evolution of the E2 glycoprotein in chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its role in host-cell attachment, immune recognition, and lineage diversification. Using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods, the research applied diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotype network analysis to characterize evolutionary pressures. Results showed that nucleotide diversity was highest in the pre-expansion period (Pi = 0.085) and lower in more recent outbreaks (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests indicated both purifying and positive selection across CHIKV E2 lineages, with lineage-specific diversifying signals observed at key codons. These findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion. The study's evidence is moderate in strength due to reliance on existing sequence data and potential biases, but it provides valuable insights for understanding CHIKV evolution and informing surveillance strategies.

title_zh: 全球遗传多样性及进化在基孔肯雅病毒 E2糖蛋白中的模式
source_body_en: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. Diversity indices, neutrality tests, and haplotypes network analysis were applied to characterize evolutionary pressures acting on E2 glycoprotein. To assess the influence of geography, host, and time on viral population structure, we performed spatial–temporal stratification and analysis to assess clustering patterns across lineages and regions using Fixation index test (Fst). Nucleotide diversity varied considerably across time, with the pre-expansion period (pre-2004) showing the highest diversity (Pi = 0.085), while more recent outbreak periods exhibited comparatively reduced diversity (Pi = 0.012). Neutrality tests revealed signatures of both purifying and positive selection across the three CKIKV E2 lineages (negatively statistically significant Tajima D, Fu and Li’s D, and Fu and Li’s F tests, p -values < 0.05) supported by codon‐based analyses showing pervasive purifying constraint across the E2 gene but recurrent diversifying signals at lineage‐specific sites, notably codon 146 in the West African lineage, codons 220, 245, 247, and 254 in the Asian lineage, and codons 54, 56, 102, 145, 163, 177, and 350 in the East/Central/South/African lineage. Population structure analyses using Fst indicated significant genetic differentiation between regional populations, reflecting restricted gene flow and localized evolutionary trajectories. Haplotype network analysis highlighted distinct clustering patterns shaped by geography and epidemic waves, reflecting the persistence of lineage-specific signatures across regions. At the same time, reduced connectivity among recent outbreak strains point to more discrete intercontinental movement events, likely driven by human-mediated vector dispersal or travel-associated introductions. Collectively, these findings underscore the spatiotemporal evolution of CHIKV E2 glycoprotein and its implications for viral adaptation and immune evasion.
